obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Primary canvas, page background, base borders — the absolute ground zero of the visual system

carbon.$description: Carbon — Card and elevated surface background, subtle border tint — the first lift off pure black

tar.$description: Tar — Deep surface fill for nested elements, icon containers — sits between canvas and card

bone.$description: Bone — Light neutral action fill for buttons on dark surfaces.

ash.$description: Ash — Muted body text, secondary headings, low-emphasis borders — warm mid-gray companion to Bone

smoke.$description: Smoke — Tertiary borders, disabled states, link underlines in rest position — the lowest visible neutral

pearl.$description: Pearl — Cool-toned secondary text, icon fills on hover, light surface highlights

graphite.$description: Graphite — Supporting text and icon borders, mid-weight border emphasis

chalk.$description: Chalk — Hairline borders, dividers, input outlines, and card edges on light surfaces. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

sans-serif.$description: sans-serif — detected in extracted data but not described by AI

nb-international-pro.$description: Primary typeface across all contexts. The 300 weight for headlines is the signature choice — most enterprise brands shout at 700; Henry whispers at 300 and achieves more authority. The 204px display weight 400 with tight tracking is unmistakably editorial, treating the product name like a magazine cover. NB International Pro's geometric humanist forms carry warmth without friendliness — it is NB Studio's workhorse, not a generic grotesque.

nb-international-pro-mono.$description: Used at 10px for metadata, tags, and technical annotations in the product UI mockup — the mono variant signals 'this is a system label, not marketing copy'

inter.$description: Secondary UI font for dense body contexts, form labels, and table-like content. Inter's wider x-height handles small sizes better than NB International Pro. The -0.037em tracking at 12px compensates for Inter's tendency to look loose at caption sizes.
